bounded_objective: Extend the fixed-terminal retained-U theorem to a genuine changing-core hierarchy and determine whether its rare charges admit one depth-independent single-use physical payment.
method: Compute the exact upper-set law for a rare switch between arbitrary disjoint sibling cores, reduce all nonterminal terms to two defect rates, prove a scalar constant, and telescope node charges and selector influences through an arbitrary finite fresh tree.
prior_status: A fixed arbitrary terminal core could be transported through arbitrarily many fresh activation controls with constant C_star<4.947, but changing cores could incur a fixed new charge at every layer.
mathematical_delta: For every fresh rare switch between arbitrary Boolean functions on disjoint sibling variable blocks, proved J<=C_sep I_ctl with C_sep<16.964. The signed charges telescope through every finite fresh read-once separated hierarchy, giving U(root)-sum_leaf w_leaf U(leaf)<=C_sep I_sel(root), independent of depth and rarity. Arbitrary leaf U packets are retained exactly once. The first unpaid term is the shared-variable Fourier overlap defect.
